items.summary: A single underperforming GPU can stall distributed training jobs while passing health checks, so NVIDIA introduces the open-source DSX OS to configure, certify, and monitor accelerated Kubernetes clusters. Its AICR tool pins version-locked configuration recipes with dependency graphs and per-component health assertions; NVCRE validates readiness by running NCCL and Nemotron tests against thresholds like busBandwidthGBps >= 300; and NVSentinel monitors continuously without consuming GPU time, quarantining faulty nodes via CEL rulesets. The three Apache 2.0 tools aim to make configuration, validation, and recovery repeatable across a cluster’s lifecycle.
items.title: NVIDIA DSX OS Certifies and Monitors Kubernetes GPU Clusters

items.summary: Google announced today that it is rolling out Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, now generally available across the Gemini API and Google for business. The update adds native video creation up to 15 seconds long, multi-turn conversational editing, and stronger reference adherence. Its price drops 30% from the previous version, reaching $0.07 per second for 720p video. Google says businesses, startups, and creatives are already using it in their workflows, backed by enterprise-grade infrastructure and an imperceptible SynthID watermark on outputs. Development continues to improve fast sports action, rapid script changes, and complex physics.
items.title: Google rolls out Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash with longer clips and lower price

items.summary: NVIDIA argues that high bandwidth memory is now contested by how much useful work each byte delivers, not just capacity. It presents Figure 1 data showing Vera Rubin NVL72 holding 288 GB per GPU while rising to 19.2 TB/s bandwidth and delivering up to 30x the throughput per megawatt of GB300 NVL72 at 160 tokens per second per user, citing SemiAnalysis AgentX. The article then walks five co-designed levers: NVFP4 precision shrinking weights by about 3.5x versus FP16; Wide expert parallelism spreading MoE experts across many GPUs; Dynamo distributed serving with KV Cache Runner and NIXL offloading to SSDs or host memory, validated in separate tests reaching up to 270 GB/s aggregate read throughput on eight H100 GPUs; the Vera CPU parking context in up to 1.5 TB of LPDDR5X during tool-call gaps; and CMX pod-level Ethernet-attached flash claiming up to 5x higher tokens per second for long-context inference versus traditional storage. NVIDIA concludes these levers stack because they are one memory system rather than independent parts.
items.title: NVIDIA Frames Co-Design as the Path to More Useful Bytes in AI Factories

items.summary: John Nack, a senior product manager at Google Cloud, announced that the AI model Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is now generally available on Google Cloud. The model targets high-volume business videos such as product clips, virtual try-ons, and advertisements, offering faster generation, lower cost, longer up to 15-second clips, stronger adherence to image and video references, higher-resolution drafts with upscale options, more natural speech, and in-conversation editing. Pricing for 720p video is stated at $0.07 per second, described as about 30% less than the previous version. Google notes that audio references require allowlisting and outputs carry a SynthID watermark. Several companies including Artlist, FLORA, invideo, Krea, Picsart, Photoroom, and QuickFrame AI shared quotes describing their use of the model across creative workflows, advertising production, and content generation.
items.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash for video creation and editing

items.summary: Google announced today that it is rolling out Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, now generally available across the Gemini API and Google for business. The update adds native video creation up to 15 seconds long, multi-turn conversational editing, and stronger reference adherence. Its price drops 30% from the previous version, reaching $0.07 per second for 720p video. Google says businesses, startups, and creatives are already using it in their workflows, backed by enterprise-grade infrastructure and an imperceptible SynthID watermark on outputs. Development continues to improve fast sports action, rapid script changes, and complex physics.
items.title: Google rolls out Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash with longer clips and lower price

items.summary: Greg Brockman, OpenAI’s co-founder and president, said the company could be ready for an IPO in 2027 while speaking at a Wall Street Journal tech conference. He cited strong enterprise revenue growth as the main driver, noting that annualized revenue rose 70% quarter over quarter after early-2026 quarters he called “pretty rough.” Brockman said OpenAI now feels more confident than ever about going public when it is ready, and pointed to a partnership with J.P. Morgan Chase as evidence of enterprise demand.
items.title: OpenAI President Says Company Could Be IPO Ready in 2027

items.summary: Anthropic announced Thursday that its chatbot Claude is gaining a new “Personal Finance” tool, letting users connect bank and credit card accounts through Plaid to ask questions about spending. Anthropic says access is read-only, so the tool cannot move or invest money, has no ads, and won’t train on chats. It launches in beta this week for Pro, Max, and Ultra plan users in the U.S.
items.title: Anthropic Adds Personal Finance Tool To Claude

items.summary: On November 5, 2026, Google Research researchers Paolo Di Achille and Ming-Zher Poh presented a new artificial intelligence system called AI-PPG-ACC-HTN that passively detects signs of high blood pressure using standard consumer smartwatch sensors without cuff calibration. The team validated the approach against 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring across five US sites involving 196 participants, reporting sensitivity and specificity figures for initial screening and confirmatory testing scenarios. The researchers note this is early feasibility research intended to support opportunistic clinic referrals rather than replace standard clinical diagnosis.
items.title: Google Research presents cuffless smartwatch AI for detecting hypertension signs

items.summary: The piece traces how the 'long reflection'—the extended period of collective deliberation before superintelligence arrives—has shifted from a span of thousands to possibly just weeks or months. Will MacAskill originally framed it as potentially lasting 10,000 years among billions of people. By 2026, viatopia descriptions suggested the reflective process might not need much calendar time because AI could unlock vast cognitive abundance. The author argues this change stems from conflating two types of reflection: learning facts about the world, which superintelligent systems can accelerate greatly by generating arguments and evidence in parallel; and becoming wiser—changing what people value—which requires actual experience, engagement, and practice that cannot be delegated or handed over as knowledge. Because deferring to AI on values would mean surrendering authorship of our own future selves, the length of reflection remains partly a choice about participation rather than something machines can simply compress.
items.title: Reflection May Shorten as AI Speeds Decisions

items.summary: Metrocon Holdings corrected its account of former chairman Alvin Lim’s dealings with the Ministry of Manpower over an unlicensed foreign worker dormitory run by LBD Engineering at 58A Sungei Kadut Loop between July 2025 and January 2026. The company said earlier statements relied on information supplied by Lim, who resigned after being charged in October to answer the charge and was released on bail. It revised interview dates for Lim and non-executive director Charlotte Tay Tingyin, his wife, whom the board cleared to remain with safeguards including a written undertaking and abstention from reappointing decisions. Metrocon said developments were not expected to materially affect operations or financial performance for the year ending Dec 31; its shares closed on Nov 5 at 22 cents, down 4.4%. A court hearing is set for Dec 17.
items.title: Metrocon revises timeline of Alvin Lim dormitory probe, keeps wife as director

items.summary: At ECML PKDD in Naples, Amazon senior applied scientist Hamed Karimi and colleagues received the 2016 paper award for their work on linear convergence under the Polyak–Łojasiewicz condition. The result helped unify scattered optimization methods that had gone largely unused since 1963. Karimi noted they did not expect it to gain traction, while original author Boris Polyak remarked he was surprised by its importance. Researchers have since applied variations of the method across standard algorithms and fields including reinforcement learning and diffusion models; the paper has been cited over 2,000 times and appears in graduate textbooks.
items.title: Karimi's Decade-Old Optimization Paper Earns Test-of-Time Recognition

items.summary: A Databricks blog explains three data-sharing methods that have emerged: OpenSharing, Clean Rooms, and Marketplace. The choice depends mainly on the relationship with whoever is on the other side of the data. OpenSharing lets recipients get direct read-only access to live assets without pipelines or copies. Clean Rooms let two businesses combine proprietary data in an approved space where only agreed code runs. Marketplace is a public storefront for offerings any customer can discover, unlike the first two options that require knowing your recipient ahead of time. The same business may use different tools across relationships.
items.title: Databricks Compares Three Data Collaboration Tools for Different Relationships

items.summary: In June 2026, Databricks and the Linux Foundation announced that Delta Sharing has evolved into OpenSharing, an open, vendor-neutral protocol for sharing data tables plus agent skills, AI models, and unstructured data. The change addresses interoperability with Apache Iceberg REST Catalog clients and on-premises or private cloud storage without migrating data first, while keeping existing Delta Sharing integrations compatible through a Share → Schema → Asset hierarchy. Databricks Co-founder Matei Zaharia said the move extends open sharing to the full AI stack; Linux Foundation CEO Jim Zemlin described it as a common framework for exchanging AI assets securely across platforms. OpenSharing is at the sandbox stage under the Linux Foundation AI & Data Foundation, with some capabilities still early stage.
items.title: Databricks and Linux Foundation Launch OpenSharing Protocol

items.summary: Chris Alexiuk, a Toronto-based senior product research engineer in deep learning at NVIDIA who specializes in open large language models, advocates for openly sharing knowledge about the technology. He teaches on YouTube and styles himself 'No. 1 Nemotron Fan' after referring to NVIDIA's Nemotron family of open source multimodal models as the most important AI project available. Alexiuk argues that fully open source AI is necessary for democratizing intelligence, giving users access to weights, training data, and recipes. He likens Nemotron to a magical library offering spells for various tasks, serving developers from individuals using Nemotron 3.5 Lightning to companies deploying Nemotron Ultra.
items.title: Chris Alexiuk Promotes Open AI Models Through YouTube Teaching

items.summary: As larger models, longer contexts and agentic applications increase GPU memory pressure while supply tightens and prices rise — a trend expected to continue through the near term — NVIDIA points to full-stack codesign rather than simply packing more memory onto GPUs. The company says it designs GPUs, CPUs, networking, storage and software together so each byte of high-bandwidth memory does more useful work across an AI factory's memory hierarchy. It cites figures from SemiAnalysis AgentX showing HBM capacity per GPU rising roughly 3% while agentic throughput per dollar rose by up to 30x on the Blackwell Ultra-to-Vera Rubin path, and tokens-per-second-per-dollar climbing faster than capacity across generations. The claims are NVIDIA's own; no independent verification is offered beyond a cited analysis benchmark.
items.title: NVIDIA Frames Full-Stack Codesign as Its Answer to AI Memory Pressure

items.summary: Across Texas, Ohio, Georgia and other states in the November 2026 midterms, voters repeatedly rejected data center expansion. In thirteen states from Florida to Maine, ballot measures restricting or prohibiting construction passed by wide margins; in Ohio several cleared more than 70% of the vote. Democratic candidates-elect including James Talarico, Gina Hinojosa and Keisha Lance Bottoms called for tax breaks to end, moratoriums on new projects and federal regulation. Pro-data center spending from a network linked to Leading the Future reportedly spent millions in races from South Carolina to Arizona, but analysts noted it fell short of its goals as opposition grew bipartisan.
items.title: Data Center Ballot Measures Lost Across the US Midterms

items.summary: A new report from the Global Disinformation Index, titled “Monetizing Hate,” estimates that about 100 English-language channels publishing hate speech could earn roughly $13.3 million in ad revenue in 2026: $7.3 million for creators and $6 million for YouTube. The authors argue enforcement is weak because it costs time while inaction does not, and note the platform’s repeat-offender clause lacks a defined trigger. They call for transparency reports that measure demonetized money rather than takedowns, citing existing EU law under Article 17 of the Digital Services Act. GDI estimates US creators account for 81% of revenue while EU users saw ads on sampled videos.
items.title: GDI Report Finds Hate Speech Still Earns Millions on YouTube

items.summary: A community forum urges greater reporting of possible child abuse, following recent news reports on fatal cases including two babies abused to death between 2021 and 2024. Author Lim Soo Ping frames the local community as the first line of defence and proposes that MSF raise public awareness and encourage residents to report concerns to its child protection service, likening it to the police’s Neighbourhood Watch Scheme introduced in 1981. The proposal is presented by one author without official confirmation from MSF.
items.title: Community Forum Calls for Neighbourhood Reporting of Child Abuse

items.summary: Land Transport Authority Group Director Tan Lijun responded to feedback by reaffirming firm enforcement against illegally modified vehicles, including heavily tinted windows. From 2023 to 2025, LTA issued more than 4,000 summonses annually for illegal modification offences. Motorists face fines up to $20,000 or imprisonment of up two years, with doubled penalties for repeat offenders.
items.title: LTA Cracks Down on Illegally Modified Vehicles and Workshops

items.summary: Mistral AI announced an expansion of Mistral Studio on Tuesday (date-62), adding managed agents, enhanced workflows, enterprise context, agent observability and evaluations to its enterprise AI platform. The release pairs with the Le Chonk model—Mistral Large 4—which the company describes as strong for coding, defensive cybersecurity and document reasoning. Customers such as ABANCA, Accenture, Alten, BNP Paribas, Capgemini, CMA CGM and Tata Consultancy Services already use Studio in production (s12). Mistral notes that one product operations team saved about 35 hours a week routing ideas from internal teams and customers (quantity-4837-4845), though the company hedges this figure. The platform lets teams deploy agents, workflows and apps across cloud, VPC or on-premises environments while retaining control over their data.
items.title: Mistral Expands Studio With Managed Agents, Workflows and Apps

items.summary: After Democrats won both chambers of Congress in the November midterm elections, spot gold rose more than 2% to US$4,138 an ounce on Nov 4 while Wall Street stocks rallied as the US dollar dipped. The Straits Times reports that analysts attribute the reaction to expectations of slower fiscal spending and reduced political uncertainty. Zavier Wong of etoro noted gold remains down over 4% this year, though he expects it back at US$4,500 in months ahead. Charu Chanana of Saxo said equities reflected easing political risk, while Steven Chiavarone highlighted that the S&P 500 has avoided losses for 12 months after midterms in 88 years. Ninghui Liu of State Street cautioned investors not to overread the dollar's decline amid ongoing expectations of Fed rate hikes.
items.title: Singapore investors weigh gold, stocks and dollar after US midterms

items.summary: Researchers from Apple present amortized maximum inner product search with learned support functions at ICML, arguing that generic MIPS methods assume queries resemble keys even though retrieval-augmented generation uses short user questions against long curated text. They propose training small neural networks once offline to route queries faster and more accurately than centroid-based routing in inverted file index systems. SupportNet learns a convex support function per cluster for better routing scores; KeyNet directly predicts the best-matching key vector as a query rewriter, keeping existing indexes intact. Both are trained by regression on Natural Questions partitioned into 128 clusters over roughly 2.6 million passages. Results show learned routers reach high recall at lower latency and fewer scanned keys than centroid baselines across increasing model sizes from XS to L.
items.title: Apple Researchers Propose Learned Routers for Faster Retrieval

items.summary: Shares in Elon Musk's SpaceX plunged more than 9% as tech and artificial intelligence stocks fell a day after Democrats won the midterms, dragging the Nasdaq down by more than 5%. The market reacted to possible tougher scrutiny of data centre construction following Democratic gains in states like Texas. Susannah Streeter said the sell-off was sending shockwaves into other markets.
items.title: Tech and AI stocks fall after Democrat midterm wins

items.summary: The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite is on track for its worst day in 18 months after slumping by up to 5% Thursday, as investors feared tougher regulation of the artificial intelligence industry following midterm elections. Chip stocks led losses, with SanDisk down 19% and Western Digital falling 16.5%. The Dow fell more than 1,000 points to 52,264. Analysts cited Democratic gains in gubernatorial races as a likely slowdown for datacentre expansion plans.
items.title: Nasdaq Braces for Worst Day in 18 Months Amid AI Regulation Fears

items.summary: On November 5, 2026, Paul Ford quoted a collection of recent articles on his website. The list includes pieces about Qwen 3.8 27B running on laptops, the U.S. Census Bureau paired with Super Intelligence, an October inflection point for vibe coding, and a battle drones game.
items.title: Paul Ford Quotes Qwen and Super Intelligence Articles

items.summary: Alexis Ohanian, Reddit cofounder and founder of venture firm Seven Seven Six, says building social media apps is “not cool anymore” as much of the internet has been compromised. He sees a better version of user-generated content emerging like group chat. His firm manages over $1.3 billion in assets under management. Reddit shares fell 29 percent last week after Google’s AI search hurt referral traffic, and Ohanian worries commercialized conversations are full of “bullshit.” Yet he remains optimistic about medical breakthroughs from the technology.
items.title: Reddit Cofounder Warns Social Apps Are No Longer Cool

items.summary: After Democrats won trifectas in Arizona, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin this week, advocates say the midterms could trigger a new era of state-level clean energy policy. The article rests on interviews with officials from Climate Cabinet, Clean Wisconsin and other groups, whose plans remain prospective rather than enacted. In Wisconsin, Erik Kanter of Clean Wisconsin expects utilities to plan for renewables; David Weiskopf anticipates a possible 100% clean electricity standard. Pennsylvania’s Senator Lindsey Williams hopes appliance-efficiency bills move forward with Governor Josh Shapiro on board, alongside $1.5 billion in transit funding. Arizona legislators led by Lauren Kuby target utility regulator reform and groundwater rules. The piece notes slim majorities may limit the window before control flips back. Figures are drawn from interviews; no laws have passed yet.
items.title: Democratic trifectas open clean-energy window in three states

items.summary: BYD launched the second-generation Seal 07 in China on Thursday, starting at around $23,000. The vehicle is roughly Camry-sized yet adds substantial technology and premium features for its price. It offers battery electric and plug-in hybrid powertrains across five variants, with an EV version delivering up to 481 miles of range and a 0-to-62 mph time of 5.5 seconds, plus fast charging from 10% to 70% in about five minutes.
items.title: BYD Unveils Tech-Packed Seal 07 EV Starting Near $23,000

items.summary: On November 5, 2026, the Federal Reserve Board announced the termination of an enforcement action against Allegiant United Holdings, LLC; Nano Financial Holdings, Inc., and Nano Banc. The agreement was dated February 24, 2021, and it terminated October 21, 2026. All three entities are based in Irvine, California. Media inquiries were directed to the board's press contact.
items.title: Federal Reserve Board Terminates Enforcement Actions Against Three Irvine Entities

items.summary: On Nov 5, Bloomberg News reported that Microsoft is tightening oversight of data center projects from neocloud providers Nebius, IREN and Nscale. Shares fell in afternoon trading, with Nebius and IREN down more than 13 per cent and CoreWeave down 11 per cent. The Windows maker says it is stepping away from risky projects while focusing on expanding its own data centers.
items.title: Microsoft Tightens Oversight of Neocloud Data Center Projects

items.summary: Parents of a US girl sued Google, claiming its Gemini chatbot was pushed onto students without warning and failed to flag suicide risks. The 13-year-old user, Emma, reportedly planned her own funeral with the bot before school software flagged it. The lawsuit seeks monetary damages in California federal court. A Google spokesperson said the company is reviewing claims while highlighting safety features built with experts; Google will disable Gemini by default for student accounts.
items.title: Google Sued Over AI Chatbot Use on School Laptops

items.summary: Elon Musk's SpaceX is partnering with Qualcomm to build a large-scale mobile network in the United States, reportedly its biggest 5G deal. The work may begin in 2027 across tens of thousands of sites, potentially challenging AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile. Qualcomm declined to state the agreement's total value.
items.title: SpaceX and Qualcomm Partner on US 5G Network Deal

items.summary: Tata Motors' connected car apps, IRA 2.0 and IRA.EV, face a cybersecurity scare after CERT-In flagged four high-severity vulnerabilities that could let hackers steal authentication credentials, impersonate owners and access vehicle information. Karan Dhar of Business Today reports the risks and Tata's response. The company says it addressed them through software updates and enhanced security measures.
items.title: Tata Motors Addresses Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities in Connected Car Apps

items.summary: At a Geneva event, WTO Director-General Amelie Ottenberg Okonjo-Iweala said the ocean economy is valued at US$ 2. 6 trillion and supports around 133 million jobs, while more than 80% of globally traded goods travel by sea. She stated there is no trade-off between prosperity and sustainability, noting that 72 per cent of world goods trade still takes place on WTO most-favoured-nation terms despite geopolitical turbulence. Okonjo-Iweala highlighted the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies, which entered into force in September 2025, and urged members to complete Fish 2 negotiations.
items.title: WTO Director-General Urges Trade Partnerships for Resilient Ocean Economy

items.summary: The Bank of England raised its base rate from 3.75% to 4%, the first increase in over three years, with eight MPC members voting for it while Catherine Mann wanted a larger half-point jump. Governor Andrew Bailey signalled possible further rises unless the Middle East conflict is resolved, noting oil has stayed above $100 a barrel and UK inflation could reach 4.9% by mid-next year. Healey’s budget offered £100 energy payments to twenty million households as cushioning measures while analysts warn of continued pressure into December or February.
items.title: Bank of England Hikes Rates Amid Iran Conflict Inflation Fears

items.summary: At least 22 flights were diverted or landed in emergencies Thursday after bomb threats, renewing questions about a coordinated effort to disrupt travel across Italy, Ireland, the UK and other European countries. The warnings affected carriers including Ryanair, Aer Lingus and easyJet; all aircraft landed safely with searches finding nothing suspicious. Iata condemned the disruption, while EU transport commissioner Apostolos Tzitzikostas said it was too early to know if incidents were linked but any threats against civilians are unacceptable. Aviation experts noted such a number of credible threats may point to coordinated action.
items.title: Bomb threats disrupt flights across Europe amid hybrid war fears

items.summary: The UK government has launched an eight-week consultation proposing national standards for shared e -bike schemes, including on-the-spot fines for riders caught drunk or riding dangerously. The plans aim to curb what ministers call the “wild west” of e-biking, where a patchwork of local rules leaves pavements unsafe for pedestrians and wheelchair users. Operators may also be required to manage fleets better, provide designated parking, take out insurance and share data with local leaders.
items.title: UK consults on crackdown against drunk and dangerous e-bike riders

items.summary: A new National Association of Realtors report finds the share of first-time homebuyers remains near a record low of 22%, as a housing shortage and high prices sideline many. Those who do buy are older and wealthier, with 1 in 10 paying all cash — a record since data collection began in 2003. NAR reports the median age of first-time buyers is 40, up from 38 for financed buyers and 54 for those paying all cash. Jessica Lautz attributes this to inheritances driving purchases.
items.title: Record Share of First-Time Homebuyers Pay All Cash Amid Housing Shortage

items.summary: Harmeet Dhillon, Assistant Attorney General and head of the justice department's civil rights division for about 18 months, is leaving her post. Attorney General Todd Blanche announced she accepted the resignation in a statement on X. She departed after midterm elections gave Democrats control of Congress, raising expectations that they will investigate executive agencies including the justice department.
items.title: Controversial Civil Rights Chief Resigns as Democrats Gain Power

items.summary: President Santiago Peña announced his resignation after Ueno Bank entered insolvency, freezing operations and blocking millions from accessing accounts. Lawmakers accused him of conflicts of interest as a former shareholder; he rejected the claims. Congress voted to pursue an impeachment trial. In a video message on X, Peña said his resignation was meant to protect stability, social peace and democratic institutions. Ueno Bank reported about three million customers, roughly 60% of Paraguay's adult population. He won election in 2023 for the Colorado Party.
items.title: Paraguay's President Resigns After Bank Collapse

items.summary: British actor-comedian Russell Brand was convicted Thursday in Southwark Crown Court of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women on allegations dating back more than 20 years. Judge Joel Bennathan said he faces a significant prison term when sentenced Monday and rejected bail due to flight risk. Brand, 51, denied the charges but showed no emotion as the verdict was read.
items.title: Russell Brand Convicted of Rape, Sentenced to Prison

items.summary: The National Development and Reform Commission, with the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and three other departments, issued an action plan to promote resource conservation and accelerate China's green transition. It targets reducing energy consumption per unit of GDP by around 10%, water use by 10%, and construction land use by 15% by 2030 from 2025 levels, plus raising recyclable-resource recycling to 510 million tonnes annually by 2030. NDRC's Li Zhong said the measures support carbon peaking before 2030 and neutrality before 2060.
items.title: China Unveils Resource Conservation Action Plan

items.summary: At the 16th World Socialism Forum in Beijing, European left-wing political figures highlighted the Communist Party of China's commitment to self-reform as a model for their own parties. Kaivon Kjems of Denmark and Adam Barbato Shoufani of Swiss Communist Youth argued that disciplined party building enables people-centric development. The forum gathered more than 80 participants from 40 countries over two days in October, according to CGTN reporting on Tuesday and Wednesday.
items.title: European left-wing figures praise CPC self-reform commitment at socialism forum

items.summary: The Metropolitan Police are investigating comedian Russell Brand over rape allegations from two additional women, it can now be reported. He was previously found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault at Southwark Crown Court in October 2026, but acquitted on other charges. Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy said more victims may come forward after the verdicts. The investigation, Operation Actinolite, took over 340 witness statements; allegations were non-recent, dating back up to 27 years, with no CCTV or forensic evidence available.
items.title: Russell Brand Faces Rape Investigation Over Two New Complaints

items.summary: Three senior figures from Aleksandar Vucic's regime boarded an Air Serbia flight to Moscow on November 3, when the crew was told to return them after entering Lithuanian airspace. Unofficial reports say Vulin allegedly skipped mandatory security screening. The episode fell just nine days before the student-backed Students' List won a landslide election victory over the SNS, ending 14 years of ruling dominance. In its aftermath, prosecutors launched investigations into electoral manipulation and corruption; Davor Macura was arrested on suspicion of removing about €383 million ($430 million) from Alta Bank's vault. Prosecutors warn that speed must not compromise evidence or final convictions as Serbia tests whether it is breaking with its old system.
items.title: Serbia's Post-Election Crackdown Follows Moscow-Bound Flight of Regime Figures

items.summary: In Casavalle, a vulnerable neighborhood on Montevideo's outskirts, Uruguayan priest Pablo Coimbra walks through half-finished homes built with concrete floors and aluminum-framed windows amid tin shacks. The district is set to welcome Pope Leo XIV this weekend. Founded in 1987, Our Lady of Guadalupe Parish has improved children's education and offers daily contact families lack from the state. Residents feel excluded yet excited about the visit. Coimbra leads Mass for 200 people weekly and distributes social aid monthly while preparing facilities including a ramp still unfinished due to damp weather. The parish continues its work regardless of the brief papal attention.
items.title: Uruguayan Priest Prepares Casavalle Neighborhood for Papal Visit

items.summary: Chemical manufacturer 3M will pay up to $7.35 billion over nine years to settle lawsuits from as many as 120,000 people who say they were harmed by groundwater contamination tied to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances linked to firefighting foam. Under the terms, payouts begin with $50 million this year, followed by yearly payments of more than $1 billion each year from 2028 to 2033. 3M did not admit liability under the agreement.
items.title: 3M Reaches $7.35 Billion PFAS Groundwater Settlement

items.summary: Jeremy Hansen, the first non-American astronaut on the Moon via Artemis 2, has become adviser and ambassador for Moon World Resorts, a Canadian company planning a giant lunar replica with up to 12,000 luxury residences across 24 towers. Sandra Matthews, its president, describes it as “the blueprint for a smart city,” costing about $5 billion at roughly $500 per 90-minute walk and millions already raised. The promoters stress that all talks remain exploratory: no meetings with governments or an investor have been held. Hansen defends the project’s engineering credibility while noting only visionaries are interested.
items.title: Canadian Lunar Astronaut Leads Madrid Moon Development Project

items.summary: A live blog tracks US midterm election results, focusing on Mississippi and Alaska contests where Democrats are gaining ground. Katherine Clark confirms she will run for House majority leader, becoming the first woman to hold the role if successful.
items.title: Midterm races on knife-edge as Republicans reel

items.summary: A London jury found British comedian Russell Brand guilty on Thursday of one rape and three sexual assaults, involving four women between 2005 and 2009. He was also cleared of two rapes and an attempted indecent assault charge. The 51-year-old will be sentenced Monday after being remanded in custody. Judge Joel Bennathan warned Brand faces a significant custodial term.
items.title: Russell Brand Found Guilty of Rape and Three Sexual Assaults

items.summary: Students marched through Athens demanding more education funding, repairs and smaller classes. Some carried banners borrowing France's 'Study or survive?' slogan; others dumped rubble from deteriorating schools to show poor conditions. Police put turnout at about 4,000 across Athens and Thessaloniki combined, well below the 20,000 who marched in 50 Greek cities on 21 October; organisers disputed the figure. Students cite rents of 800 euros a month as they call for housing allowances and rent caps.
items.title: Greek Students Rally for Education Funding

items.summary: Iran's leadership has largely dismissed the significance of Republican losses in the US midterm elections, with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warning that concessions or partisan changes are unlikely to end American hostility toward Iran. Journalist Mohammad Sadegh Javadi Hesar said Tehran would not alter its position over a shift in Washington. Some officials read the results more favorably: Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf claimed Americans rejected war, while hardline media dismissed party differences as meaningless for Iranian policy. Analyst Hossein Alizadeh sees US politics affecting global dynamics but considers large-scale military escalation unlikely.
items.title: Iranian officials downplay US midterm results amid regional tensions

items.summary: Nvidia shares fell more than 6% to around $186 in early Thursday trading, potentially the first close below $200 since July 30. The drop follows concerns that slower data center construction could reduce orders for Nvidia's processors and networking equipment. Despite the decline, analysts maintain bullish targets averaging about $333, while Nvidia reports strong revenue growth forecast at 70% for fiscal 2028. Its next earnings report is scheduled for November 17.
items.title: Nvidia Shares Drop Below $200 on Data Center Fears

items.summary: The Kerala government launched the Sabari portal and a WhatsApp chatbot to provide pilgrims with real-time updates on darshan, transport, accommodation, healthcare and emergency services as preparations begin for the Mandalam-Makaravilakku pilgrimage season. Revenue Minister A P Anilkumar inaugurated the platform Thursday; it was developed by Pathanamthitta district administration. The portal offers complaint reporting forwarded to police control rooms, location-based facility information, darshan waiting times and pilgrim counts, KSRTC integration and price monitoring at shops in Pamba, Nilakkal and Sannidhanam. District Collector A Nizamudeen said the initiative would improve inter-departmental coordination. The 41-day-long Mandalam pilgrimage season commences on November 17.
items.title: Kerala Launches Digital Portal for Sabarimala Pilgrims Ahead of Mandalam Season

items.summary: Senior Indian auto parts executives say major tariff changes are unlikely unless US-India trade talks progress, since Democrats can override a presidential veto with a two-thirds majority. The US accounts for 26% of India's overseas auto shipments, and total exports reached $24 billion in FY26 per the Automotive Component Manufacturers Association (ACMA). Tariffs stood at about 2% before Trump-era revisions, while USTR opened a Section 301 probe into alleged unfair practices. There has been no resolution so far.
items.title: Indian Auto Parts Makers Await Trade Talks for Tariff Relief

items.summary: Last month, Apple lowered the daily spending cap for some engineers using AI models to $200 from $300, according to people with knowledge of the change. The company now plans further cuts, potentially reducing allowances to as little as $100, though actual savings remain unclear since many employees did not use their full limits.
items.title: Apple Cuts Employee AI Spending Caps Amid Cost-Cutting Push

items.summary: Three works—Kalhana's 'Rajatarangini', the 'Mahabharata' and Kautilya's 'Arthashastra'—were added to Unesco's Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the committee, held in Jakarta, Indonesia. In 2024, India had already secured recognition for three other literary works: The Ramcharitmanas, Panchatantra and Sahṛdayālokalocana.
items.title: India's Rajatarangini, Mahabharata and Arthashastra Gain Unesco Memory of the World Recognition

items.summary: Chennai Super Kings and Sunrisers Hyderabad struck one of the biggest deals of the IPL 2027 trading window, sending Liam Livingstone and Jack Edwards to CSK while Khaleel Ahmed and Nathan Ellis join SRH. The headline move is that of Livingstone, who was bought by SRH for Rs 13 crore, and an official statement by the tournament says he now joins CSK at less than half that price – Rs 6 crore.
items.title: CSK and SRH Trade Four Players in IPL 2027 Deal

items.summary: Jailed activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have separately approached the Supreme Court challenging the Delhi High Court's September 30 order refusing them bail in the larger conspiracy case over the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots, which left 53 people dead. Both argue the prosecution has examined no witness despite more than six years of custody and that a one-year filing window is ending.
items.title: Khalid and Imam Challenge Delhi HC Bail Refusal at Supreme Court

items.summary: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation reported a 57.3 per cent rise in standalone net profit to Rs 15,489 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27. The company credited higher crude oil realisations from nominated fields, which rose 37.1 per cent to USD 92.33 per barrel. ONGC also awarded offshore development projects worth Rs 11,800 crore and approved an interim dividend of Rs 8 per share.
items.title: ONGC Posts Sharp Q2 Profit Jump on Higher Oil Prices and Offshore Wins

items.summary: President Santiago Peña resigned on Thursday amid growing calls for his removal after digital lender ueno collapsed, leaving roughly 3 million customers unable to access accounts. Lawmakers accused him of conflicts of interest and misuse of pension funds; he lost backing from members of his own party earlier that day. Vice-President Pedro Alliana is set to replace him.
items.title: Paraguay President Resigns After Digital Lender Ueno Collapse

items.summary: A Gujarat municipal clerk, Mahesh Vasava of Dabhoi Municipality in Vadodara district, was suspended for six days after 12 streetlights along a road used by Prime Minister Narendra Modi were found non-functional and others flickering. The suspension order cites alleged negligence despite repair instructions under Section 48 of the Gujarat Municipalities Act, 1963. Vasava must appear before the competent authority on November 6 at 11 am to explain himself; his extra duties have been withdrawn.
items.title: Gujarat Clerk Suspended After Streetlights Fail on Modi's Route

items.summary: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman released a ₹250 commemorative coin on Tuesday marking the 250th birth anniversary of Carnatic music maestro Muthuswami Dikshitar at Banaras Hindu University in Varanasi. The event, organised under IIT-BHU's Centre of Excellence for Indian Knowledge Systems with support from the Bombay Stock Exchange's CSR programme, featured musical tributes and student interactions. Sitharaman said: "It is important to familiarise children with India's rich cultural traditions." Commemorative coins are minted in limited quantities as memorabilia rather than currency.
items.title: Finance Minister Releases Dikshitar Commemorative Coin

items.summary: Two leaders of Essex charity Kidz Come First were jailed after diverting £315,000 in donations meant for disabled and terminally ill children. Ruksana Khan was sentenced to five years and 11 months; James Donovan received three years at Chelmsford Crown Court on 13 June 2024. Investigators traced funds to online gambling and household bills. Essex Police are seeking confiscation orders to recover the money, describing the theft as shocking.
items.title: Essex Charity Founders Jailed for £315,000 Donation Theft
